name: fill_me
title: Human-readable target name
description: What this coverage analysis is trying to measure.

coverage_focus.purpose: Which concrete coverage slice under project_spec this target analyzes.
notes: Keep target-specific coverage-slice decisions here. Keep project implementation details in specs/*.json.

scope_in: List the architecture areas, Spike components, instruction classes, or behavior classes that belong in this target.
scope_out: List exclusions so scripts can filter obvious noise and the agent can avoid proposing out-of-scope tests.
line_priority_regex: regex terms that should rank line-level functions higher for this target
analysis_notes: Optional notes for the agent about how to interpret coverage evidence for this target.

scenario_coverage.purpose: Optional target-owned guidance for architecture-visible cross execution scenario coverage. Use these fields as a reporting checklist, not as a Cartesian product to enumerate blindly.
evidence_policy: Line/branch/call/entry coverage is supporting evidence, not the test intent.
Do not claim a cross scenario is covered unless same-flow evidence exists.
Derive cross scenario signatures from target scope, Spike source, .gcov, single-case deltas, or path-marker records.
Do not generate a blind Cartesian product from scenario_axes.

path_analysis.purpose: Optional path-aware evidence policy. Use this to describe how the agent should report and prove execution-flow coverage when gcov branch/call coverage is not enough.
evidence_policy: Do not treat path_analysis as a complete path matrix or architecture specification.
Derive path signatures from Spike source and gcov evidence; do not invent combinations from a predeclared Cartesian product.
Use path_signature_fields only as a reporting checklist.
If all relevant edges are covered only in aggregate, mark edge-covered-path-unknown.
Use single-case increment evidence or per-instruction/access path markers before claiming same-flow path coverage.

marker.name.meaning: What this marker proves when emitted by an instrumented Spike.

required_practice: Run one tiny single-purpose case after resetting or snapshotting coverage counters.
Compare before/after .gcov snapshots for required line/branch/call counter increases.
Use Spike -l --log-commits when useful to confirm the target guest instruction executed.
interpretation: If a required edge/call stays zero, the path is confirmed not executed.
If required counters increase but isolated-case/log/profile evidence is incomplete, mark counter-increment-observed instead of single-case-increment-confirmed.
If all required counters increase in a tiny single-purpose case and Spike log/profile evidence confirms the target instruction, mark single-case-increment-confirmed.
If edges are covered only in aggregate, mark edge-covered-path-unknown.

marker_correlation_policy: Strong marker evidence requires JSON per-instruction/access records with pc+insn, seq, or access_id correlation fields.
JSON records without correlation fields and text fallback records are weak evidence only.
Marker sequence observation is evidence; the agent must still validate marker placement and architectural observable.

example shared paths.gate_note: manual/special-run unless the selected platform makes this deterministic
